newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill bullish on Intel, Micron.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill bullish on Intel, Micron.

text.p: -- Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlak said on Wednesday the drop in semiconductor stock prices was close to ending and consensus estimates for Intel Corp and Micron Technology Inc earnings were too low.

-- "Strong personal computer sales to businesses is driving Intel's sales mix to higher-performance processors, helping to increase its average selling price and reducing dependence on consumers," Kurlak wrote in a report.

-- "We believe the semiconductor stock price correction is nearing an end as stronger fundamentals come into focus and earnings estimates increase. Consensus estimates are believed to be too low on Intel and Micron."
-- Kurlak said there was pent-up demand for Intel's new Pentium II chip. "We look for a large backlog for the chip by late summer in the corporate market."
-- DRAM prices are up in response to production cuts by South Korean companies, strong demand, low inventory and dumping charges by Micron, he said.
-- "We expect Micron to meet our earnings targets of $0.21 a share in FQ2 (the fiscal second quarter), $0.45 in FQ3, $0.75 in FQ4 and $1.50 for the year ending in August.
-- "Our FY 1998 estimate is $3.50. Consensus estimates are lower."

-- On Intel, Kurlak wrote, "We believe our earnings estimates of $9.30 for 1997 and $11 for 1998 are conservative, but are above the consensus, which we believe is too low. The primary driver to our estimate is revenue growth, which is expected to approach 50 percent this year."
-- Intel rose 1-3/4 to 148. Micron rose 3/4 to 40-5/8.
